description: The best Android tablets you can buy in the United States under five hundred dollars: live prices from Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart and Samsung.com, with screen-size and stylus advice so you do not spend the cap on a case instead of a tablet.

heroBody: In the United States, five hundred dollars is the line between a media tablet and a work tablet. Under that cap you are looking at Samsung Galaxy Tab A and last-gen Tab S FE Wi-Fi models, Amazon Fire HD 10 for video-only households, and the occasional Galaxy Tab S9 Wi-Fi open-box that dips into this band. These are US-dollar prices sold into the United States. This page pulls live listings from BuyWhere's catalog so you can see what Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart and Samsung's own store are charging today — and skip the flood of screen protectors and cases that share the same search terms.

highlightSectionTitle: What US shoppers should know at this cap

highlights.title: Search results are drowning in cases
highlights.body: US catalog search for Galaxy Tab S9 still surfaces privacy films and book-style cases priced in the same band as real tablets. If a listing is a screen protector or folio, ignore it — this page's product cards are meant to be the tablets. When in doubt, required terms and a floor price are how we filter.

highlights.title: Wi-Fi vs cellular is the real money decision
highlights.body: A US-unlocked LTE/5G Galaxy Tab often jumps over five hundred dollars even on last-gen FE silicon. If you use the tablet at home or on cafe Wi-Fi, buy Wi-Fi only and tether from your phone on the rare day you need a cell radio.

highlights.title: Fire OS is not Android, and that matters for sideloading
highlights.body: Amazon Fire tablets are cheap and excellent for Prime Video. They do not run the Play Store without extra steps, and those steps break on OS updates. If you need Kindle plus YouTube Kids plus a school Chromebook-class browser, Galaxy Tab A is the cleaner US buy.

highlights.title: S Pen in the box is how FE earns the top of this cap
highlights.body: Samsung's FE Wi-Fi models often include the S Pen. Paying extra later for a stylus on a Tab A usually costs more than starting on FE. If you never write on screen, save the money and stay on Tab A.

adviceSectionTitle: How to stay under five hundred without buying a case by accident
advicePoints: Read the title for 'Wi-Fi' versus '5G'. Cellular SKUs at this cap are often carrier-locked or last-gen warehouse stock.
Skip listings whose primary photo is a folio, glass film, or keyboard. Those are accessories riding the tablet query.
Prefer Amazon sold-by-Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, or Samsung.com. Grey imports may be other-region firmware without US LTE bands.
If you want DeX or a stylus, start on Tab S FE Wi-Fi rather than adding a keyboard to a Tab A.
Kids' tablets: Fire HD with a case and a parental profile is still the US default. Do not buy a Galaxy Tab S for a seven-year-old unless you want to replace a cracked OLED.
faqSectionTitle: Android tablets under five hundred dollars in the US — questions shoppers actually ask

faqs.question: Can I get a Galaxy Tab S9 in the US for under $500 in 2026?
faqs.answer: The base Wi-Fi S9 sometimes lands here as open-box or warehouse. New Plus and Ultra models do not. The live cards on this page are the current US floor.

faqs.question: Is an Amazon Fire tablet a real Android tablet?
faqs.answer: It is a fork. Video and reading are excellent. Full Play Store apps are not guaranteed. If you need Android apps as sold, buy a Galaxy Tab A.

faqs.question: Should I buy from Samsung.com, Best Buy or Amazon?
faqs.answer: Samsung.com is cleanest for FE + S Pen bundles and education SKUs. Best Buy wins on in-store returns. Amazon wins on Fire tablets and sold-by-Amazon Galaxy A models.

faqs.question: Do I need LTE on a tablet under $500?
faqs.answer: Usually no. Phone hotspot covers travel. LTE adds cost and often a worse Wi-Fi configuration at this budget.

categoryIntro.heading: Why US sub-$500 Android tablet search is messy
categoryIntro.body: Samsung's US catalog shares model strings between tablets, privacy glass and book covers, so a naive search looks well-stocked while the actual Wi-Fi tablets hide one scroll down. Amazon's Fire line uses different OS branding again. This page is a live catalog pull with accessory exclusion rather than a static 'best of' list that ages out after a Back-to-School sale.
